    Classes:

    Name Description
    BatchBase

    Base interface for dataset-like collections of structured samples.
    BatchSampler

    Read-only batch wrapper that samples mini-batches from another batch.
    SpaceStorage

    SpaceStorage is an abstract base class for storages that hold instances of a specific space.
    SegmentWriter

    Builds one contiguous segment of a storage off to the side.
    BufferedSegmentWriter

    Keeps the appended samples in memory and writes them with one set() on commit.
    MappedSegmentWriter

    Forwards to a writer of an inner storage, mapping every appended sample with transform.
    ToBackendOrDeviceBatch
    CombinedBatch
    SliceStackedBatch

    A batch that stacks frames with given fixed offsets.
    FrameStackedBatch

    A batch that stacks frames in a sliding window manner.
    SubIndexedBatch

    A batch that offers a view of the original batch with a fixed index range.
    SubItemBatch

    A batch that offers a view of the original batch with a fixed index.
    TransformedBatch
    StepSampler

    Samples mini-batches of individual steps (uniformly, with replacement) from data.
    MultiprocessingSampler
    ReplayBuffer

    Ring-buffer style batch storage built on top of a SpaceStorage.
    ReplayBufferCollectionWrapper

    Automatically record every transition into one or more replay buffers.

    BatchBase ¶

    BatchBase(
    single_space: Space[BatchT, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType],
    single_metadata_space: Optional[
        DictSpace[BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType]

    Bases: ABC, Generic[BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType]

    Base interface for dataset-like collections of structured samples.

    BatchBase stores the per-sample space definition and provides a uniform API for retrieving either structured values or their flattened backend-array representation. Concrete subclasses decide where data lives and which mutation operations are supported.

    Initialize the batch contract for one logical sample.

    SpaceStorage ¶

    SpaceStorage(single_instance_space: Space[BatchT, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType])

    Bases: ABC, Generic[BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType]

    SpaceStorage is an abstract base class for storages that hold instances of a specific space. It provides a common interface for creating, loading, and managing the storage of instances of a given space. Note that if you want your space storage to support multiprocessing, you need to check / implement __getstate__ and __setstate__ methods to ensure that the storage can be pickled and unpickled correctly.

    Bind the storage to the space of one stored element.

    Create a new storage instance for samples from single_instance_space.

    shrink_length

    This is used by capacity = None storages to shrink the length of the storage
    get

    Read one or more samples from storage.
    set

    Write one or more samples into storage.

    A writer that builds one segment of this storage off to the side; see SegmentWriter.
    clear

    Clear all data inside the storage and set the length to 0 if the storage has unlimited capacity.
    dumps

    Dumps the storage to the specified path.
    close

    SegmentWriter ¶

    SegmentWriter(storage: SpaceStorage)

    Bases: ABC

    Builds one contiguous segment of a storage off to the side. Values appended to a writer land at an index range that is only chosen when the writer is committed, so several writers of one storage can be filled at the same time (e.g. one per environment of a batched rollout) and committed in any order. Obtain one with SpaceStorage.open_segment_writer().

    Methods:

    Name Description
    append

    Append one structured sample to the segment.
    finish

    Declare the segment complete (no more appends) and release what only appending needs (e.g. encoders).
    commit

    Write the segment to the storage indices [start_index, start_index + len(self))
    abort

    Drop the segment without writing it.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    storage
    length
    is_finished

    get_column ¶

    get_column(nested_keys: Sequence[Any]) -> BatchBase

    Lazy view over one field of the samples that combines the children's column views, so that children able to read a single column cheaply (replay buffers, stacked views, ...) do so instead of fetching whole samples. Values, spaces, metadata and the flattened layout are those of SubItemBatch(self, nested_keys), which is returned when the children's column views cannot be combined. The view is read-only.

    fill_data_with_stack_mask ¶

    fill_data_with_stack_mask(
    space: Optional[Space[Any, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType]],
    data: Union[BArrayType, BatchT, Any],
    valid_mask: BArrayType,
) -> Union[BArrayType, BatchT, Any]

    Fill the data with the mask as if the frames were frame-stacked.

    data is updated in place where the backend allows it (backend.at(...).set; JAX and read-only arrays are copied). This is safe because data is the result of fetching an index array from the wrapped batch, a fresh gather: batches wrapped by a SliceStackedBatch must not return arrays aliasing their storage from get_at* / get_flattened_at* with index arrays. Args: space (Optional[Space]): The space to fill the data with. If None, the data is assumed to be a backend array. data (Union[BArrayType, BatchT, Any]): The data to fill sized (B, T, *D) valid_mask (BArrayType): The mask to fill the data with, sized (B, T) Returns: Union[BArrayType, BatchT, Any]: The filled data, sized (B, T, *D)

    get_column ¶

    get_column(nested_keys: Sequence[Any]) -> BatchBase

    Lazy view over one field of the stacked samples.

    Stacks self.batch.get_column(nested_keys) instead of stacking whole samples and dropping the other fields afterwards, so only that column (plus the episode column the built-in valid-mask helpers read) is gathered. Values, spaces, metadata and the flattened layout are those of SubItemBatch(self, nested_keys), which is returned when that is not possible (a custom valid mask function, which may read any field, a mask read from metadata, or a column view with different metadata).

    close ¶

    close() -> None

    Release this view. The wrapped batch is not owned by the view and stays open; close it through whoever created it (BatchBase.__del__ calls close(), so closing the source here would tear it down whenever a view is garbage-collected).

    FrameStackedBatch ¶

    batch: BatchBase[BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType],

    postfetch_horizon: int = 0,

    ] = None,

)

    Bases: SliceStackedBatch[BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType]

    A batch that stacks frames in a sliding window manner. This batch allows for prefetching and postfetching of frames, which can be useful for training models that require temporal context (e.g. Diffusion Policy, ACT, etc.) This is a read-only batch, since it is a view of the original batch. If you want to change the data, you should mutate the containing batch instead.

    StepSampler ¶

    StepSampler(
    data: BatchBase[BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType],
    batch_size: int,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    device: Optional[BDeviceType] = None,
)

    Bases: BatchSampler[BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType, BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType]

    Samples mini-batches of individual steps (uniformly, with replacement) from data.

    Performance notes:

    • For data held in RAM (e.g. an in-memory ReplayBuffer and views over it), sampling in-process is usually faster than MultiprocessingSampler: worker processes only pay off when producing a batch is expensive (decoding, transformations, storage reads), since every batch is copied to the main process.
    • sample_flat() / get_flattened_at() flatten a sample into one array of a common dtype, so uint8 images next to float32 fields are cast to float32 (4x the bytes and a conversion per batch). Prefer sample() for image data.
    • Read single fields through data.get_column(keys) rather than sampling whole samples.

    MultiprocessingSampler ¶

    MultiprocessingSampler(
    sampler: BatchSampler[
        SamplerBatchT,
        SamplerArrayType,
        SamplerDeviceType,
        SamplerDtypeType,
        SamplerRNGType,
        BatchT,
        BArrayType,
        BDeviceType,
        BDtypeType,
        BRNGType,
    ],
    n_workers: int = 4,
    n_buffers: int = 8,
    ctx: Optional[BaseContext] = None,
    doze_time: float = 0.005,
    daemon: Optional[bool] = None,
    shared_memory: bool = False,
)

    Bases: BatchSampler[SamplerBatchT, SamplerArrayType, SamplerDeviceType, SamplerDtypeType, SamplerRNGType, BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType]

    Run sampler's sample* functions (and epoch iteration over its get*_at functions) in n_workers background processes, keeping n_buffers batches queued.

    Workers pay off when producing a batch is expensive (decoding, transformations, storage reads). For data already in RAM (e.g. an in-memory ReplayBuffer), sampling in-process is usually faster (e.g. 0.7 ms vs 3 ms for 256 samples of 48 KiB with 4 workers): every batch is otherwise copied to the parent through shared memory. Workers run their torch ops single-threaded (see _limit_worker_intraop_threads).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    shared_memory bool

    For sample() / sample_with_metadata() of samplers producing torch CPU tensors, workers copy each batch into one of n_buffers + 1 pre-allocated shared-memory slots and the parent copies it out, instead of sending every tensor through the result queue (a new shared-memory file and file descriptor per tensor and batch). This pays off when batches arrive at a high rate (e.g. ~2x for 64 samples of 48 KiB); for large batches the copy out of the slot in this process can cost more than it saves, so it is off by default.

    		 False

    ReplayBuffer(
    storage: SpaceStorage[BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType],
    storage_path_relative: str,
    count: int = 0,
    offset: int = 0,
    cache_path: Optional[Union[str, PathLike]] = None,
    multiprocessing: bool = False,
    *,
    maintain_segment_metadata: bool = False,
    physical_segments: Optional[Sequence[Tuple[int, int]]] = None,
    active_segment_start_physical: Optional[int] = None,
    active_segment_length: int = 0,
)

    Bases: BatchBase[BatchT, BArrayType, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType]

    Ring-buffer style batch storage built on top of a SpaceStorage.

    The buffer exposes the standard BatchBase interface while handling round-robin overwrite semantics, persistence metadata, and optional multiprocessing-safe counters.

    With multiprocessing=True writers serialize on a shared lock and publish count and offset together; readers in other processes take no lock and always map indices with a consistent pair. A read that races with a write can still return rows that the write is overwriting (the oldest samples of a full buffer), as with any lock-free ring buffer.

    Wrap a storage object with replay-buffer indexing semantics.

    open_segment_writer ¶

    open_segment_writer() -> SegmentWriter

    A writer that builds one segment off to the side; commit_segment() then appends it at the tail. Unlike append() / mark_segment_end(), any number of writers can be open at a time (e.g. one per environment of a batched rollout), and they can be committed in any order. Storages that support it (e.g. VideoStorage) encode the samples as they are appended.

    ReplayBufferCollectionWrapper(
    env: Env[
        BArrayType,
        ContextType,
        ObsType,
        ActType,
        RenderFrame,
        BDeviceType,
        BDtypeType,
        BRNGType,
    ],
    replay_buffers: Union[ReplayBuffer, Sequence[ReplayBuffer]],
    replay_mode: Literal["auto", "shared", "per_env"] = "auto",
    transition_builder: Optional[Union[Callable[..., Any], DataTransformation]] = None,
    validate_transition: bool = False,
    dump_on_episode_end: bool = False,
    dump_on_reset_boundary: bool = False,
    dump_path: Optional[PathLike] = None,
)

    Bases: Wrapper[BArrayType, ContextType, ObsType, ActType, RenderFrame, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType, BArrayType, ContextType, ObsType, ActType, RenderFrame, BDeviceType, BDtypeType, BRNGType]

    Automatically record every transition into one or more replay buffers.

    Parameters¶

    env : Env The environment to wrap. replay_buffers : ReplayBuffer | Sequence[ReplayBuffer] One replay buffer (shared mode) or one per environment slot (per‑env mode). replay_mode : "auto", "shared" or "per_env" * "shared" - a single flat replay buffer. * "per_env" - one buffer per batched slot, with episode segments. * "auto" - resolve based on batch_size and buffer count. transition_builder : callable or DataTransformation, optional Either a callable (cached_obs, cached_context, action, next_obs, reward, terminated, truncated, env_index, rb_single_space) -> transition, or a DataTransformation that maps a canonical raw transition dict to the replay buffer's format. When None the default DictSpace‑based builder is used. validate_transition : bool When True every built transition is validated against the target replay buffer's space (single‑instance for append / batched for shared extend). Off by default for speed. dump_on_episode_end : bool When True, automatically call dumps(path) on the replay buffer(s) after an episode ends (i.e., when terminated or truncated is true). Requires dump_path to be set. dump_on_reset_boundary : bool When True, automatically call dumps(path) on reset boundaries (full reset or masked reset). Requires dump_path to be set. dump_path : str | os.PathLike | None Filesystem path where the replay buffer(s) should be dumped when auto-dump is triggered. May be reassigned after construction to redirect subsequent dumps. Required if dump_on_episode_end or dump_on_reset_boundary is True. Repeated dumps overwrite the same path.

    require_same_space: bool = True,
    allow_mid_episode: bool = False,
    finalize_old_segments: bool = False,
    dump_old: bool = False,
) -> List[ReplayBuffer]

    Swap the replay buffer(s) without rebuilding the wrapper.

    Parameters¶

    replay_buffers : ReplayBuffer | Sequence[ReplayBuffer] The new replay buffer(s) to use. replay_mode : "auto", "shared", "per_env", or None If provided, change the replay mode. If None, keep the current mode. require_same_space : bool If True, the new buffers must have the same single_space as the old buffers. Default is True. allow_mid_episode : bool If True, allow swapping even if this splits an episode across old/new buffers. Default is False. finalize_old_segments : bool If True, close any open segments in the old buffers before swapping. Default is False. dump_old : bool If True, dump the old buffers before swapping. Requires dump_path to be set. Only does this safely after segment finalization where needed. Default is False.

    Returns¶

    List[ReplayBuffer] The old replay buffer(s) that were replaced.

    Raises¶

    ValueError If the new buffers don't match the expected layout or space. RuntimeError If there are open segments and allow_mid_episode and finalize_old_segments are both False.
